question_text: A 46-year-old woman comes to the physician for a follow-up examination. She had a blood pressure recording of 148/94 mm Hg on her previous visit one week ago. She is 160 cm (5 ft 3 in) tall and weighs 52 kg (115 lb); BMI is 20 kg/m2. Her pulse is 88/min and blood pressure is 150/96 mm Hg. Cardiopulmonary examination is unremarkable. Serum concentrations of electrolytes, creatinine, lipids, TSH, and fasting glucose are within the reference range. A urinalysis is within normal limits.
